newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine denies Falklands policy comment.
newsitem.headline: Argentine denies Falklands policy comment.

text.p: Argentina denied Tuesday British media reports that an Argentine minister had predicted London would soften its stance on the Falklands dispute in the likelihood that the Labour Party wins the May 1 election.

The specialist magazine Jane's Defence Weekly was due to run a story Wednesday quoting Argentine Defence Minister Jorge Dominguez, who is very close to President Carlos Menem, saying British policy would change if the Labour Party wins.

But the Argentine Foreign Ministry said Dominguez "at no point presumed the new government will be Labour nor that the results of the upcoming elections will ensure a change in position of the United Kingdom, though he did express a wish that the latter will happen."
Britain and Argentina fought a 10-week war in the remote South Atlantic islands in 1982 after Argentina sent troops to try to enforce its long-standing sovereignty claim.
About 1,000 troops, mostly Argentine, lost their lives before Britain won back the islands.

The two former foes restored diplomatic ties in 1989 and have forged close trade ties, but Britain refuses to even discuss sovereignty of the Falklands, while Menem insists he will win back the islands for Argentina by 2000.
Foreign Minister Guido Di Tella has led a diplomatic offensive to win the islanders' trust with stunts that have included sending them greetings on Queen Elizabeth's birthday.
The Argentine statement said Di Tella, in his talks with the ruling Conservatives and Labour, had seen "no substantial differences between them" on the Falklands issue.
But Di Tella trusted that whatever the result of May 1's vote, "the new administration will have a sufficient majority to hold a constructive and fruitful dialogue on the future of the islands."
